title: Finite coproduct product cone for point Kan extensions
statement: Use the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let X be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] with small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Let a_X be the relative profinite test-object functor of [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-test-object-functor]. Let C be any category and F a C-valued sheaf on profinite spaces for finite jointly surjective covers. Let P be a presheaf on X.ProEt, with a unit eta from F to a_X.op followed by P, exhibiting P as a pointwise left Kan extension. For every finite family (U_i) of affine objects, assume that for every epimorphism A → B of sheaves of sets on X.ProEt the induced map A(U_i) → B(U_i) is surjective. Then there exists a cofan c of the U_i which is a colimit in X.ProEt, and the cone with point P(c.pt) and legs P((c.inj i).op) is a product cone in C. This includes the empty family.

source.place: Lemma 4.2.13(1), proof, component-factorization and sheaf argument; finite-coproduct consequence in RefactorInstruction Section 4, Lemma point-eval

proof.text: Construct W as the scheme coproduct of the U_i, with structure morphism Sigma.desc of their structure morphisms. Weakly etale is Zariski local at the source (Mathlib IsZariskiLocalAtSource.sigmaDesc), so W is an object of X.ProEt. The scheme coproduct universal property gives a colimit cofan c in X.ProEt.

By [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-point-components-maps], write T_i for the profinite component space of U_i and b_i for the natural equivalence between maps U_i → a_X(S) and maps T_i → S. Form their finite coproduct T in Profinite, with inclusions j_i. The two coproduct universal properties give a natural equivalence b_W(S) between maps W → a_X(S) and maps T → S, characterized by j_i ≫ b_W(S)(f) = b_i(S)(c.inj i ≫ f).

For V = U_i and V = W, let q_V be the inverse image of the identity under b_V(T_V). Naturality and injectivity of b_V say that every f : V → a_X(S) uniquely equals q_V ≫ a_X.map(b_V(S)(f)). This makes (T_V,q_V) terminal in CostructuredArrow a_X.op (op V). The pointwise Kan cocone has an invertible leg there (Mathlib IsColimit.isIso_ι_app_of_isTerminal). Its inverse gives e_V : P(V) ≅ F(T_V), normalized by eta_S ≫ P(f.op) ≫ e_V.hom = F(b_V(S)(f).op). Precomposing with all Kan cocone legs at W and using the restriction identity of the preceding step proves P((c.inj i).op) ≫ e_i.hom = e_W.hom ≫ F(j_i.op).

A coherent sheaf on Profinite preserves finite products on the opposite (Mathlib Presheaf.instPreservesFiniteProductsOppositeVal). Apply isLimitFanMkObjOfIsLimit to the opposite of the coproduct cofan of the T_i. The e_V and their compatibility from the preceding step identify this limit with the desired restriction cone. For an empty family the coproduct T is initial and its image under F is terminal, so the same argument proves the empty case.

lean.statement:
theorem point_lan_finite_products (X : Scheme.{u}) (C : Type w) [Category.{v} C]
    (F : Sheaf (coherentTopology Profinite.{u}) C) (P : X.ProEtᵒᵖ ⥤ C)
    (η : F.obj ⟶ (profiniteToProEtOf X).op ⋙ P)
    (hP : (Functor.LeftExtension.mk P η).IsPointwiseLeftKanExtension)
    (I : Type u) [Finite I] (U : I → X.ProEt)
    (ha : ∀ i, IsAffine (U i).left)
    (hw : ∀ i,
      ∀ (A B : Sheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology X) (Type (u + 1))) (f : A ⟶ B),
        Epi f → Function.Surjective (f.hom.app (op (U i)))) :
    ∃ c : Cofan U, Nonempty (IsColimit c) ∧
      Nonempty (IsLimit (Fan.mk (P.obj (op c.pt)) (fun i ↦ P.map (c.inj i).op)))
